QuitGame ends the game with an exit code: an exported game exits with it, the editor stops play mode. LoadScene replaces the running scene with a scene asset (every entity of the current scene goes away), or restarts the running scene for the null handle; it fails for assets that are not scenes. LoadSceneAdditive loads a scene asset into the playing scene next to what it holds (a sub-scene) and returns the sub-scene's ID (0 when it cannot start: not a scene asset). The asset and everything it uses load in the background; then its entities are created over the following frames (a bounded number per frame), keeping the IDs they have in the asset (a sub-scene whose IDs the scene has already fails: loading one twice). UnloadSubScene removes a sub-scene: it cancels its load or destroys its entities with their descendants (at the end of the frame, like DestroyEntity); false for an unknown ID. IsSubSceneLoaded is true once every entity of the sub-scene exists. |

A controller is an active entity with an enabled CharacterController component and no RigidBody; the functions fail for other entities, for non-finite values and while the scene plays without physics. What they set takes effect at the next fixed step. CharacterMove sets the velocity (meters per second, world space) the character walks with until the next call: the horizontal part moves it along the ground, the vertical part counts only while its GravityScale is 0. CharacterJump makes it move up at &#96;speed&#96; meters per second at its next fixed step, on the ground or not. CharacterTeleport moves it and its entity to a world position at once (its feet: the entity's origin), keeping its walk velocity and dropping its vertical velocity. CharacterGetState reads it after its last fixed step. |
